chapter: Willie Lynch, the Blue Rhythm Band and Teddy Hill
title: His first record on clarinet, 'Slow and Steady', and how the solo was made
summary: The interviewer reveals Holmes played clarinet on 'Slow and Steady' for King Oliver in 1928; the Cabin solo was a head, over a stock three-clarinet arrangement.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Actually, we discovered that your very first record, under King Oliver's name, you were also on clarinet back in 1928.
I was?
Yes.
And what was I playing then?
Well...
There you go, there you go. Well, we won't go into that right now.
Anyhow, it was our first number that we put on the tape, because it was your first recording, and you were on clarinet at that time.
"Tight Like That."
No, no. It wasn't with Russell. It was under Oliver's name.
Oh yeah? It wasn't "Tight Like That."
No. I could tell you the title.
I'm trying to think what I played. Was it solo clarinet?
Yeah, there was solo on there that you did.
I did it.
Yes.
Boy, I'm some clarinetist. I can't even
remember one number from the other, and I didn't play but two solos -- and I can't remember the other one.
"Slow and Steady" was the name of the tune.
Oh, yeah-yeah-yeah. "Slow and Steady."
So now you're back again, noodling away on the clarinet, and Irving Mills has just rushed out and said, "That's what he wanted."
Yeah. That's what he wanted. And that's exactly what he got -- what he wanted. Well, you heard it. There t'is. And that was all she wrote.
So what happened, then? Did someone write out your solo, or did you just play it?
The solo I played then?
Yeah. Did you have to make an arrangement?
No. It was just...
At that point it was just a head.
That's what he wanted. He wanted a solo clarinet. Instead of a B-clarinet, he wanted a solo clarinet with me playing...
Oh, the solo clarinet. In the lower register.
In the lower register. And that's what he got. No, wasn't nothin' written there. That was it.
Well, who had written the arrangement for three clarinets? Do you remember that?
I think it was a stock arrangement.
Oh, I see.
I think it was a stock arrangement. I don't know. I really don't know. I don't know who had written the arrangements; you know, the band arrangements.
[PAUSE]
